svg.aria-label: Chandelle profile: a 180 degree climbing turn, bank set in the first 90 degrees and held, pitch increasing to the 90 degree point, then pitch held and bank rolled out so the wings are level at 180 degrees just above stall speed

g.text: CHANDELLE — maximum performance 180° climbing turn
One continuous maneuver in two halves. Entry speed is the manufacturer's recommendation, or no more than VA — read it from the POH or AFM.
GROUND TRACK, SEEN FROM ABOVE
ENTRY
wings level,
entry speed
90° POINT
the turn reverses course
FIRST 90° — PITCH CHANGES
Roll smoothly to the bank you have
chosen and hold that bank constant.
Add power to the setting the POH gives
and raise the nose steadily, so pitch is
still increasing all the way round.
Highest pitch attitude is at the 90° point.
SECOND 90° — BANK CHANGES
Hold the pitch attitude constant and
roll off the bank at a steady rate.
Airspeed bleeds off through this half,
so rudder pressure keeps increasing.
Wings level exactly at 180°, just above
a stall, and hold it a moment.
PITCH AND BANK THROUGH THE MANEUVER
PITCH — rises, then held
BANK — set, held, then rolled off
Completion standards: the rollout is complete at the 180° point ±10° of heading, at an airspeed just above a stall, and you
maintain that attitude momentarily. The ACS sets no altitude or airspeed number here — the grade is on the shape of the maneuver.
